newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on soybeans, China offer.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on soybeans, China offer.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on a drop in soybean futures and on offers of corn by China into the world market plus commercial selling, traders said.
"The fact China offered small quantities of corn in the world market gave reason to sell corn," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.

Traders in Seoul Monday said South Korean feed millers are likely to purchase 450,000 tonnes of corn for April arrival this week. The traders said there was a distinct possibility they may buy some of this corn from China rather than the U.S.
Commercial selling was noted in corn futures.
ADM Investor Services sold three million bushels of March, Cargill Inc sold two million March and Tenco Inc sold 1.5 million March as did Hagerty Trading, traders said.

Corn futures were underpinned by fund buying, estimated at least 11.0 million bushels. Rosenthal Collins and Iowa Grain each bought six million bushels of March and Refco Inc bought four million bushels of March.
Corn closed one to 3-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with March down 1-1/2 at $2.71-3/4.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 68,000 contracts, above the 44,449 traded Friday.

In corn options, Refco Inc sold 300 May $2.70 calls at 10-1/2 to 11 cents, Rand Financial bought 300 May $2.70 puts and sold 300 July $3.00 calls at 2-1/2 cents and Spike Trading sold 300 July $2.70 puts at 13 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 18,000 contracts, above the 15,172 traded Friday.
